answer: An agent economy can blunt a Sybil attack by making every identity pay a non-refundable registration bond, priced the same for all. A swarm of fake agents must post that bond per identity, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand bonds, each slashed on misbehavior. This turns cheap identity into a real inlet of capital attackers cannot refill, and the cost scales with accounts, not with one. Honest agents spread their weight like a zephyr, unaffected by the swarm. Trust then accrues as a slow tide, rewarding long-lived members.
